location.description: an evidence-only DRAFT pre-release of NicoTM77/Mandatary (tag name `p120-evidence-v2`, no tag exists until a draft is published and it must never be published): not a product release and not a C5 release. A draft is visible to repository writers only; it is read through the GitHub API with `gh` (see docs/release-acceptance.md). The older draft `p120-evidence-v1` is left unchanged.

notes: Git history limit: the raw evidence files were committed at f306a2a and fbb8193 of this pull request and are removed at the branch tip by additive commits. Their Git objects stay in the repository's history (the pull request's commits remain reachable through refs/pull/25/head) and are NOT purged; no history was rewritten. If the pull request is squash-merged they are not in main's history; the archive, not Git history, is the durable record.

An evidence-only draft release is durable for as long as the repository and the draft exist; an administrator can edit or delete it. The member manifest and the tarball digest committed here make any change detectable by the full audit; they cannot prevent deletion.

Version 2 supersedes version 1 without changing it: its manifest contains every one of the 131 members of `p120-evidence-v1` with the identical SHA-256 (`ARCHIVE.p120-evidence-v1.sha256` is the committed v1 manifest, so `report.py --check` proves this from the two manifests without reading either archive). v1 stays available in its own draft release.

dispositions.decision: The existing interleaved A/B evidence is accepted as the owner-authorized disposition of R2, and SH-2d may be PASS WITH EXPLICIT DISCLOSURES once the report, criteria and disposition are consistent and independently reviewed. This is an acceptance-policy amendment, not a statistical result. No further statistical experiment and no broader behaviour change is part of this disposition.
dispositions.kept_visible: proof-drop runs 2/15 (arm A, no cache) against 0/30 (arm B, bounded continuity cache), one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.106 (original target p < 0.05 NOT met); contended `REL-LOAD-STABLE` passed in 0/15 A runs and 30/30 B runs, with 669 against 0 timeouts and 191 against 0 refusals of granted calls; clean 10 + 10 runs met every target (metadata reads per call -92.8 %, /info -99.8 %, daemon CPU per call -86.4 %, p95 not worse, 0 refusals/drops/timeouts in B); the original clean-host failures (3 of 5 VM runs, 18-68 % refusals) were NOT exactly reproduced in 16 later clean runs of the pre-cache product, although the mechanism (daemon saturation amplified by the service's own continuity reads, every proof drop a failed daemon read with about 50 calls in flight) is evidenced; the causal uncertainty is not removed. All clean and adverse results, the orphan arm-A contended run (kept, not counted) and the smoke-B run are preserved in the archive.
dispositions.not_claimed: that the pre-registered drop-rate statistic passed; that the original failures are exactly reproduced or exactly explained; any security waiver. Authorization, identity, invalidation, cancellation and fault classification, leases and freshness semantics are unchanged by this disposition; every denial that is a genuine unsafe or uncertain identity result stays a denial.

dispositions.residual_risk: Under a saturated daemon the service can still refuse a legitimate call (403 safety_unverified, default_deny) or time out a daemon read: the failure is fail-closed (an availability risk, not an integrity or confidentiality risk), it is logged by the safety-transition diagnostics (`docker safety proof dropped` / `restored`, closed reason, no secret), and it is rarer and shorter with the bounded continuity cache (0 drops in 30 contended B runs).

findings.detail: technical-decisions.md 10.2 states the idle budget as "after startup" without a duration. In steady state the service is well inside it (27.8 MB after a first start, 33.3 MB when configured, 27.2 MB after a restart; `vm-amd64/release.json`, `footprint.idle`), and `REL-FOOT-SETTLE-*` passes. But every start (first start, restart, SIGKILL restart) first holds about 100 MB (100.55 MB peak after the first start, 98.81 MB after a restart) until 145-155 s, i.e. roughly twice the budget for two and a half minutes; the same figures were measured on both hosted CPUs (98-99 MB, settled at 140-160 s). It reproduces natively with the container's environment: with the SMTP relay configured, one heap allocation of about 64 MiB happens 85 ms after start (`GODEBUG=gctrace=1`: `94->94->88 MB`), and Go returns it to the OS only after the runtime's 2-minute forced collection. Not asserted here: which code path allocates it. A follow-up in the product (release the memory after the one-time work) would remove the transient; the harness records the whole curve and gates on the settle. R3 (owner decision): the steady-state definition of the idle budget (the maximum of the samples inside the final 60 s of a 300 s window) is accepted and documented in docs/release-acceptance.md; the transient itself is still reported (`REL-FOOT-SETTLE-*`).
findings.title: Start-up transient: about 100 MB resident for 2.5 minutes after every start

findings.detail: The adverse runs of the earlier rounds stay in the archive (`vm-diag-loop-1`, `vm-diag-loop-2`, `vm-run-1a01db9-full`) and stay FAIL in the criteria that name them. Evidenced (the root-cause report, archive `records/R2-RCA-report.md`; the mechanism, not the exact cause of the original clean-host failures, which was not reproduced): the fixture daemon saturates under the workload (dockerd and containerd about 165 % and 138 % of one CPU of 4) and the service multiplied its reads (12 per admitted status call, 33 per tail-logs call, every proof drop a failed daemon read with about 50 calls in flight). R2/B changed the product: one epoch-bound continuity check, at most one in flight, valid for less than 1 s, covers read admissions and stream deliveries; mutations, name resolution, target inspects and every authorization decision stay fresh (`docs/docker-backend.md`). The interleaved A/B measurement is in the archive (`diagnostics/r2-ab/README.md` is the guide): clean 10 + 10: metadata reads per call -92.8 %, `/info` per call -99.8 %, daemon CPU per call -86.4 %, p95 status 2.13 s -> 0.48 s and logs 5.99 s -> 0.49 s, 0 refusals/drops/timeouts in 10 B runs; contended (two host CPU burners) 15 A + 30 B: `REL-LOAD-STABLE` failed in 15/15 A runs and 0/30 B runs, timeouts 669 against 0, refusals 191 against 0, but the proof dropped in 2/15 A and 0/30 B runs (one-sided Fisher p = 0.106, target p < 0.05): the statistic the plan set for the drop rate alone is **not** met. The owner accepted this evidence as the disposition of R2 (section 6); SH-2d is therefore PASS WITH DISCLOSURES, not a pass of the statistic. The original clean-host failures were not exactly reproduced; the residual fail-closed availability risk is documented. The final VM run and both hosted runs of this evidence are clean (`REL-LOAD-STABLE` PASS).
findings.title: Intermittent fail-closed refusals under the approved workload on the slow VM daemon (R2): mechanism evidenced, bounded continuity cache measured, owner-approved disposition

findings.detail: `footprint.idle[configured].VmHWM_process_lifetime` is 178.07 MB on the VM (178.9 and 181.8 MB on the hosted runners): the setup, identity and matrix sign-ins (Argon2id, 64 MiB each) push the process above the 150 MB load budget briefly. The benchmark workload (API/MCP clients and log streams) contains no human sign-in and its measured peak is 41-43 MB with the high-water mark reset at the start of the window, so the budget is met as defined; a burst of sign-ins during load is not covered by this workload.
findings.title: Sign-in and setup raise the resident set to about 180 MB (outside the benchmark workload)

findings.detail: After a **clean** restore the manifest reports `agent_credentials 0` and `authenticators 2`; the two authenticators are the ones the restore itself retired locally (`restore report credentials_stripped: true`, no imported credential). docs/backup-restore.md says a clean archive carries no credential, which is true; the manifest field name suggests otherwise. The harness asserts the bearer-credential count and the report flag, not the sum.
findings.title: The restore manifest's `inactive_credentials` counts the installation's inactive records, not only the imported ones

findings.detail: (a) The hosted runners' `docker` buildx driver cannot export OCI, so on them the compressed image size is an **estimate** (every layer of `docker save` gzip-compressed at level 6; 12.29 MB amd64 and 11.66 MB arm64); on the VM the real OCI export gives 12 418 706 bytes and the estimator was calibrated against it at 0.15% on the same image (12 400 226 against 12 418 702 bytes). (b) The crash is a SIGKILL delivered to the service process from the host: `docker kill` is not used because the daemon treats it as a manual stop and never applies the restart policy. (c) The `--skip` option of the harness exists for diagnostics only; the final VM run of this evidence skipped nothing (`stage_seconds` has no `skipped`).
findings.title: Measurement notes

findings.detail: In the first VM run of the F2 fix (code commit 41ae8d5, archive `round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/vm-amd64/`) the persistence stage's re-login got a 403 on the TOTP step (`PERSISTENCE-ERROR`, 155 PASS / 2 not PASS with the REL-STOP-LONG harness defect), so the restart, SIGKILL and usage-after-crash checks of that run did not execute. The same stage passed in the next VM run at 2ac064f (156 PASS) and on both hosted CPUs. The cause is NOT established (the bare status carried no code or reason; candidates such as a TOTP step or replay-window race in the harness's re-login were not tested); the harness now records the refusal's closed code and reason and the TOTP period of the failing step (`tests/release/stackdeploy.py`, diagnostics only). A recurrence would be investigated as a possible product or harness defect.
findings.title: One unexplained `login step 2: 403` in the persistence stage of one VM run

findings.detail: The first run of the new `REL-STOP-LONG` check passed its product assertion (REST stop answered 200 after 12.2 s on the VM and on both hosted CPUs, before the fix the same shape is an EOF/502) and failed only because `tests/release/mcpclient` reported `elapsed_ms` 0 for every step (a deferred assignment on an unnamed result). The check is deliberately fail-closed on an unmeasured MCP answer; the client was fixed (named result) and the check re-run at 2ac064f. Both runs are archived (`round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/`).

remediations.adverse_run: hosted CI run 44003552068, job `Image (linux/amd64)` (head e5e1856, merge commit 0d6b022fc1d1b180092ac87fd2409a0c85422b3e): `REL-MATRIX-REST`, `REL-MATRIX-PARITY` and `REL-MATRIX-POS` FAIL, X-dn-stop-A: REST `(502, '', '')`, MCP 200. The product of that run was identical to the product the earlier evidence judged, so one of four hosted runs of that product failed. Archive root `adverse-ci-e5e1856/`; the run was omitted from the first version of this evidence (review 519 F1) and is now recorded as an adverse run of the criteria that cite those checks.
remediations.finding: Review 519 reproduced a product defect on the same call shape: `cmd/mandatary` set a 10 s `WriteTimeout` on every response while an admitted one-shot stop or restart may run `timeout_seconds` plus a 15 s stop grace (10 + 15 s by default, up to 315 s). The server closed the connection before the handler wrote its result, so the client saw EOF (behind the proxy an empty-body 502) although the stop completed and was counted allowed. The harness then recorded no per-call timing, so it cannot be shown from the archived run that its X-dn-stop-A call exceeded 10 s.
remediations.fix: Narrow, after authorization only: the ops service announces the dispatch bound of an admitted stop/restart (`ops.DispatchObserver`, only for those two operations, only after authorization and the expired-bound check); the REST and MCP transports then extend that one response's write deadline to bound plus 5 s (`api.WithAdmissionDeadline`, forward only, read deadline untouched). Unauthenticated, denied and invalid requests keep the 10 s bound. No authorization, identity, invalidation, lease or freshness semantics changed. Documented in docs/api-mcp.md and docs/operations.md.
remediations.fresh_evidence: At the code commit 2ac064f: the VM run (`vm-amd64`) 156 PASS / 0 not PASS and both hosted CPUs (`ci-amd64`, `ci-arm64`, hosted run 44059883746) 156 PASS / 0 not PASS: `REL-MATRIX-REST`, `REL-MATRIX-PARITY`, `REL-MATRIX-POS` and `REL-STOP-LONG` PASS on all three (the REST stop answered 200 after 12.2 s on every CPU). The matrix timing of the VM run shows the slowest matrix stop/restart at 5.3 s.
remediations.not_established: that the write bound was the cause of the one hosted 502: the archived run has no per-call timing and the failure did not recur (the hosted runs 44044826495 at 45629a3, 44055078430 at 41ae8d5 and 44059883746 at 2ac064f all passed `REL-MATRIX-REST`), so the cause of that single 502 is not established. The write-bound defect is real and fixed; the remediation closes the criteria on fresh passing evidence and does not prove that this was the cause. A later hosted 502 of the same shape would reopen it.
